description.description: Phase-based plan to build an internal agile ticketing system on Strapi v5, Next.js 14 + Tailwind, and PostgreSQL.

Core features are CRUD tickets, guarded member management, and deadline management; Kanban, priority, types, comments/activity log, labels, sprints, search, dashboard, notifications, attachments are added as high-value low-cost suggestions; time tracking, third-party integrations, custom workflows, multi-tenancy and SMTP invites are deferred to the backlog.

Four roles with escalating capability: Scrum Master (full CRUD on tickets, members, sprints; assign work; manage deadlines), Lead Dev (full CRUD on tickets, assign devs, update status, manage deadlines), Developer (read tickets, update only status + comments on assigned tickets), Viewer (optional read-only).

Provides JWT auth and role gating, but only gates at the controller-action level: a role can call ticket.update or it cannot. It does not natively enforce row-level or field-level authorization, so plugin permissions alone are insufficient and will leak write access.

Plugin permissions cannot express 'assignee may change only status'. Enforced via a custom ticket.update controller: row-level check that only the assignee may touch the ticket, and field-level stripping of the request body down to { status } for non-managers.
A custom Strapi policy (scrum_master | lead_dev) guards create/delete so non-managers receive 403 before ever reaching the controller.

Central entity: title (required string), description (Markdown or Blocks), status/priority/type enums, UTC-stored deadline, many-to-one assignee/reporter/sprint, many-to-many labels, multiple attachments, one-to-many comments/activities, and a string fractional-index rank for board ordering.
Time-boxed cycle: name (required), goal, startDate, endDate, status enum (planned/active/completed), and one-to-many tickets.
Scoped to user-authored collaboration content (body, author, ticket) so that system events are not mixed into the human comment stream.
Flexible grouping primitive: unique required name plus a hex color value.

Explicit audit-trail type with action enum (created, status_changed, assigned, deadline_changed, priority_changed), nullable fromValue/toValue, and actor relation. Modeled explicitly rather than overloading Comment because an explicit log is cleaner for filtering and audit; the alternative (a type:'user'|'system' field on Comment) is acknowledged but not recommended.
Adds displayName, avatar (media), title (job title) and isActive (boolean) to the built-in users-permissions.user type.

Use strapi.documents('api::ticket.ticket') rather than the deprecated v4 Entity Service; relational operations key off documentId (string) instead of the integer id, so routes and frontend fetches are designed around documentId.

Sequential integers (1,2,3...) were rejected because inserting or moving a card requires O(N) cascading writes. Storing rank as a string fractional index (generateKeyBetween(a, b) from the fractional-indexing library) makes a move a single O(1) update; ordering query is sort=rank:asc, lexicographic and stable client-side.

Strapi /api/auth/local returns the JWT in the JSON body, not a cookie. Proxying all traffic through Next.js Route Handlers / Server Actions converts it into a Secure, SameSite=Lax httpOnly cookie, eliminating CORS credential problems between localhost:3000 and localhost:1337 and keeping the JWT out of client-accessible storage (XSS exposure).
Guards protected routes by checking cookie presence; role-aware UI reads the user from a session endpoint.

Core agile UX, but requires optimistic updates and fractional ordering; built with @dnd-kit/core chosen for accessibility and keyboard capability, with drag cancellation, keyboard navigation and empty columns called out as edge cases.
Chosen for optimistic mutations and cache sync on the Kanban board, giving zero-flicker drag-and-drop instead of router.refresh().
Radix-based accessible primitives (Dialog, Select, DropdownMenu, Avatar, Badge, DatePicker) out of the box; also offsets UI cost, which is one reason the single-dev timeline is considered achievable.

Standard users-permissions create/update endpoints are never granted to tokens, because that would let any authenticated user change roles or self-escalate. A dedicated controller exposes POST /api/members/invite, PUT /api/members/:id/role and PUT /api/members/:id/deactivate, each verifying a Scrum Master / Lead Dev caller and bounding role assignment (cannot grant above the caller's role, cannot self-promote).
MVP invite avoids an SMTP dependency; the server generates a temporary password and the user is direct-added, with SMTP email invites deferred to the backlog.

deadline is a DateTime stored as UTC ISO 8601 in PostgreSQL but displayed in the user's browser local timezone (Intl.DateTimeFormat / date-fns-tz) - raw UTC is never rendered. Overdue query is filters[deadline][$lt]=<nowUTC> AND filters[status][$ne]=done. UI states: overdue red, due within 48h amber, on track neutral (shadcn Badge). Reminders deferred to MVP+ via a Strapi node-cron daily job.

ActivityLog entries on status/assignee/deadline/priority change, reporter auto-set and rank assigned on create are all written automatically by lifecycle hooks / custom controllers; client-supplied audit data is never trusted.
Phase 3 API behavior: deadline < now && status != done.
REST recommended for the MVP; GraphQL left as an optional later addition.
Markdown + react-markdown chosen for the description field because it is simpler than a Blocks AST; switch to Blocks + @strapi/blocks-react-renderer if structured content is needed.

Phase 0 env setup, 1 backend data modeling, 2 auth & custom RBAC, 3 core API behaviors, 4 frontend foundation + BFF, 5 ticketing UI, 6 member management, 7 dashboard & polish, 8 QA & deploy; all items are unchecked checkboxes, i.e. planned rather than shipped.

Revised from 10-15 days to ~13-17 days: RBAC +1d, API held at 2d, Kanban +1d, Members held at 1d. Primary bottlenecks are custom RBAC correctness and Kanban DnD edge cases; shadcn/ui offsets UI cost and resisting scope creep keeps this achievable for one dev.

Acceptance criteria: role-gated ticket CRUD, unbypassable status-only updates for developers on assigned tickets, guarded member controller with no escalation path, UTC deadlines rendered locally with overdue/due-soon indicators, Kanban with O(1) fractional rank moves, server-side activity log, JWT only in an httpOnly cookie, dashboard metrics, deployed app.

backend/ (ticket, member, sprint, comment, label, activity-log APIs plus policies/is-manager.ts) and frontend/ (BFF auth routes, [...proxy] route, board, tickets/[documentId], members, dashboard, components/ui, lib/api.ts, middleware.ts) with docker-compose.yml at root.
Time tracking / burndown charts, third-party integrations (Slack, GitHub), custom workflows per project, multi-project/multi-team tenancy and SMTP email invites are explicitly excluded from the MVP.
Open vs closed counts, overdue count and per-member load, plus a Phase 6 per-member workload view.

Phase 8 requires verifying that field/row authorization cannot be bypassed via the API, alongside a seed script, env config and deployment of Strapi (Render/Railway/VPS) + Postgres and Next.js on Vercel.
The root README contains only a title, so it carries no architecture or rationale content.

Unmodified Strapi scaffold README documenting npm run develop (autoReload on), npm run start (autoReload off), npm run build (admin panel) and yarn strapi deploy, plus deployment options such as Strapi Cloud.
Boilerplate pointers to the Strapi resource center, documentation, tutorials, blog, changelog, GitHub repository, Discord, Forum and Awesome Strapi.
Default Strapi file with the Disallow-all block left commented out, so search engines are not currently blocked; uncommenting User-Agent: * / Disallow: / would hide the site altogether.
Default create-next-app boilerplate: npm/yarn/pnpm/bun run dev, app on http://localhost:3000, edits to app/page.tsx, next/font with the Geist font family.
Boilerplate recommendation to deploy on the Vercel Platform, matching the plan's Phase 8 target of Next.js on Vercel.

Round-cornered blue square (#4945FF per Strapi brand) bearing the white Strapi glyph: an angular interlocking-flag/arrow mark built from triangular and rectangular facets with a lighter translucent overlapping square.
File name and placement at backend/favicon.png indicate the asset serves as the favicon, providing the visual identity shown in browser tabs and bookmarks for the ticketing module backend.
The mark is the default Strapi project logo, unmodified (no custom project branding), visually encoding the CMS/framework identity of the backend.
